In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the respiratory system is the main determinant of the systemic circulation, and the latter is the main determinant (or the most important determinant in the case of the pulmonary circulation) of the respiratory system, with the exception of the case of acute lung injury (ALI).
the heart, the lungs and the brain are intimately linked in a dynamic equilibrium that is essential to life.
the heart is the most important organ in the respiratory system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
respiration and systemic blood flow are intimately related.
respiration and systemic circulation are two interrelated systems that have a common purpose: to provide adequate oxygen delivery to the tissues.
the respiratory system is the main determinant of the cardiac output and of its distribution, whereas the systemic hemodynamic system is the main regulator of the cardiac output.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the understanding of cardiorespirator interactions can be greatly simplified if one considers the heart and lung as a single functional unit (i.e., the cardiopulmonary system).
the respiratory and circulatory systems are not isolated entities, but rather form an inseparable whole.
the understanding of cardiorespirator interactions is based on a few simple physiological principles, which can easily be mastered by the practicing intensivist.
